gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the two headline numbers on the $199 BLUETTI Elite 30 mini are on a different basis from the EcoFlow RIVER 3's: BLUETTI's "6,000+ cycles" carries no end-of-capacity percentage on its US page, and its "80% in 46 min" becomes 103 min to full against about an hour to full for the RIVER 3.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages (The Inertia, PowerSized Black Friday tracker) and five other results (Watt & Warden, MachineFanatic, Radar of Products, The Power Station Guide, RV Gear Lab). PowerSized lists the Elite 30 mini at $199, 288 Wh, 300 W, 7.3 lb with no cycle life, surge or recharge figure. The Inertia gives the RIVER 3 "3000" cycles with no percentage and "an hour" to full, and has no Elite 30 mini. The Power Station Guide is the nearest: it gives RIVER 3 "3,000+ (80%)" and says 600 W via X-Boost or Power Lifting is not 600 W continuous, but it has no Elite 30 mini row. ChatGPT's own answer already says the RIVER 3's 600 W boost is not continuous, so the surge point is not new. No page puts the two units' cycle or recharge claims on one basis. Limit: I could not open EcoFlow's own page or either manual, so the EcoFlow side rests on The Inertia.
decides: It confirms the Elite 30 mini as the pick on what is like-for-like (288 Wh vs 245 Wh, 7.3 lb vs 7.8 lb, both 300 W continuous), but removes two tie-breakers the 11-26 notes leaned on. "Twice the cycle life" cannot be written, because BLUETTI's page gives no threshold. "Faster recharge" holds only to 80%; to full the RIVER 3 is quicker (about 60 min vs 103 min). At one cycle a week both cycle ratings outlast 50 years, so cycle count should not rank this page; rank on watt-hours and weight.

findings.label: AC recharge, both bases

findings.note: Page gives no charging wattage or conditions. Arithmetic: 80% of 288 Wh = 230.4 Wh in 46 min, about 300 W average; the last 57.6 Wh take 57 min, about 61 W average; 288 Wh in 103 min is about 168 W average.

findings.label: Weight, UPS switchover, standby draw

findings.note: All three are BLUETTI's figures. Arithmetic: 288 Wh / 7.3 lb = 39.5 Wh per lb; 288 Wh / $199 = 1.45 Wh per dollar.
